summary.headline: ASK Automotive Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 35.3% YoY, EBITDA Rs 140 Cr (+31.1%), margin 12.1% hit by aluminium pass-through lag.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 35.3% YoY; excluding an 8% aluminium pass-through and a 2.7% wheel-assembly reduction, net revenue grew about 30%. EBITDA was Rs 140 Cr (+31.1%) with a 12.1% margin, which management says would have been 80 bps higher without the aluminium pass-through lag, and PAT was Rs 72 Cr (+24.2%). For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 16.2% (about 20.1% underlying), EBITDA was Rs 551 Cr (+24.1%) at a 13.1% margin, and EPS was Rs 15.08 versus Rs 12.56. Management says aluminium price increases in March were not fully passed on, costing a conscious Rs 5 Cr, and that April price increases have since been passed to both aftermarket and OEM customers. Wheel assembly revenue goes to nil from 1 April 2026.

+16.2% YoY (about +20.1% excluding aluminium pass-through of 3.1% and wheel assembly reduction of 7%)
Rs 1.85 per share (92.5% on Rs 2 face value)

segments.name: Advanced braking system
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 32% YoY in Q4 FY26 and 17% in FY26; management says it retains market leadership.

segments.name: Aluminium light-weighting precision solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 47% YoY in Q4 FY26 and 30% in FY26.

segments.name: Safety control cable
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 26% YoY in Q4 FY26 and 14% in FY26.

segments.name: Independent aftermarket
segments.commentary: Grew 24.7% in FY26 (about 25% per analyst), attributed to GST cut from 28% to 18% enabling share gains from grey market and duplicators.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports Rs 141 Cr vs Rs 147 Cr last year, a decline due to tariffs, geopolitics, supply chain and logistics; export target missed.

segments.name: Wheel assembly
segments.commentary: Low-margin business being strategically exited; revenue nil from 1 April 2026.

guidance_outlook: Management expects mid-teens revenue growth in FY27; the 20% export growth figure was an analyst's characterisation that management corrected to mid-teens guidance.
Management aims to sustain FY26 EBITDA margin (13.1%) and gradually improve it, with the aluminium denominator effect the main exception.
Alloy wheel revenue expected at Rs 90-100 Cr in FY27 and about Rs 220 Cr in FY28.
Management expects FY27 real growth to be about 4 percentage points above published growth, given the wheel assembly exit.
Management expects OEMs to compensate for aluminium and minimum wage cost increases; no margin pressure expected from wages.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about Rs 400 Cr, of which Rs 40-50 Cr is maintenance and the rest is new plant capacity; to be funded by internal accruals with debt kept within limits.
9.9 MW captive solar plant at Sirsa, Haryana, fully operational since April 2025.
11.55 MW captive solar plant at Bikaner, Rajasthan, expected commissioning in Q2 FY27.
Bangalore (18th plant, third Bengaluru plant) at about 90% utilisation with capacity full; Karoli plant at about 65% utilisation.
Alloy wheel first supplies to Japanese customer from Karoli plant handed over on schedule; supplies start in H2 FY27. Cable JV (GTD) plant audited by system suppliers, supplies to restart in H2.
demand_pricing: Management says the two-wheeler industry produced 26.7 million units in FY26 (23.9 million in FY25) and 7 million in Q4 (5.8 million); FY26 vehicle production grew 11.8%.
Aluminium rose from about 285 to 365 (per management); April price increases passed to aftermarket and OEM customers.
Q4 margin lag: about Rs 5 Cr unrecovered aluminium cost in March.
Management says there have been no production disruptions in Q1 FY27 and that customer orders remain robust.
EV two-wheeler revenue growing at a single-digit rate in FY26; Ola volumes declined, partly offset by other customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any margin deficiency beyond the 80 bps aluminium pass-through impact in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is only the aluminium timing issue; about Rs 5 Cr was conceded in March, and April increases were passed on to aftermarket and OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 margin outlook and two-wheeler industry volume expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: OEMs are maintaining production schedules; management expects to hold the 13.1% FY26 margin, with absolute FY27 numbers unchanged in the aluminium-volatile case.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital negative in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Naresh Kumar attributed it to the late-March aluminium spike, which raised receivables because invoice pricing lagged; he expects normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and its breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 400 Cr in FY27: Rs 40-50 Cr maintenance, the rest for new plant capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35% Q4 growth beyond price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 30-year track record of outperforming the industry and new products and customers; joint ventures are expected to contribute from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the alloy wheel and sunroof ventures be in the mid-teens guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that new products and customers are included in the mid-teens guidance, with JV supplies starting in H2.

risks_watch: Aluminium price volatility and pass-through timing; a repeat of the March lag would compress Q1 FY27 margins.
West Asia geopolitical conflict affecting exports (FY26 exports fell) and input costs.
Possible ABS mandate; management said it knows of no current update.
Monsoon risk to two-wheeler demand; management said it cannot quantify the impact.
Ramp-up timing of alloy wheel (Japanese customer) and sunroof/cable JV supplies in H2 FY27; alloy wheel revenue of Rs 90-100 Cr is needed for FY27.
Negative working capital from receivables build-up at year-end; management expects normalisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, order books and outgrowing the industry, but cautious on margins and geopolitics. Management deflected the ABS mandate question as hypothetical and corrected an analyst's 20% growth figure to mid-teens guidance.
key_quotes: There was a conscious loss by us of Rs. 5 Cr because every day we cannot increase the prices and the prices were rising actually every day.
We are confident that will continue to grow around mid-teens in FY27.
We have not given you 20% guidance, we have given you mid-teens guidance.
